title: Associated primes of a nonzero principal quotient of a normal Noetherian domain
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $a\in A$ be nonzero. An associated prime of $A/aA$ means a prime ideal equal to the annihilator $\{r\in A: r\bar c=0\}$ of some nonzero $\bar c\in A/aA$. Every such associated prime $\mathfrak p$ has height one: $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$, and there is no strict chain of prime ideals of length greater than one ending at $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: Notation and lower bound. Let $\mathfrak p$ be an associated prime of $A/aA$, so $\mathfrak p=\operatorname{Ann}_A(\bar c)$ for some nonzero $\bar c\in A/aA$. Since $a\bar c=0$ in $A/aA$ we have $a\in\mathfrak p$, and $a\neq0$, so $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$; as $A$ is a domain, $(0)$ is a prime ideal, and $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ is a chain of length one ending at $\mathfrak p$. It remains to show there is no strict chain of primes of length $\ge2$ ending at $\mathfrak p$.

proof.text: $A$ has $(S_2)$. Let $A_{\mathfrak q}$ be the localization at any prime $\mathfrak q$; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] it is a normal domain, so $A$ is a normal ring in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. $A$ is Noetherian, so Serre's criterion [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal] gives that $A$ has $(R_1)$ and $(S_2)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk]; in particular $\operatorname{depth}(A_{\mathfrak p})\ge\min\{2,\dim(A_{\mathfrak p})\}$.

proof.text: $(S_1)$ for $A/aA$ at $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-in-ses] (2) applied over the Noetherian local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ to the sequence of step 3, $\operatorname{depth}(M)\ge\min\{\operatorname{depth}(A_{\mathfrak p}),\operatorname{depth}(A_{\mathfrak p})-1\}=\operatorname{depth}(A_{\mathfrak p})-1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. So if $\dim(A_{\mathfrak p})\ge2$, then $\operatorname{depth}(A_{\mathfrak p})\ge2$ by step 2, and $\operatorname{depth}(M)\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 031T, proof of (1), second sentence ((S_2) for R gives (S_1) for R/aR via Tag 00LX lemma-depth-in-ses, part (2))

proof.text: An associated prime gives depth zero. Since $\operatorname{Ann}_A(\bar c)=\mathfrak p$, [lem-weil-pbc-associated-prime-localize-at-prime] (with $T=A$, $P=A/aA$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p$) gives $\operatorname{Ann}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}(\bar c/1)=\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$, so the maximal ideal $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ is an associated prime of the finite $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module $M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-dim-associated-prime] over the Noetherian local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$, $\operatorname{depth}(M)\le\dim(A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p})=0$, the quotient being a field, whose only prime is $(0)$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Hence $\operatorname{depth}(M)=0$.

proof.text: Conclusion. Steps 4 and 5 give $\dim(A_{\mathfrak p})\le1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], $\dim(A_{\mathfrak p})$ is the supremum of the lengths $t$ of strict chains $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_t$ of primes of $A$ with $\mathfrak p_t\subseteq\mathfrak p$; in particular there is no strict chain of length $\ge2$ ending at $\mathfrak p$. With step 1, $\mathfrak p$ has height one.
